title: Fractions on a number line
examples: How do I show a fraction bigger than one on the number line?
What does it mean to divide the line into equal intervals?
If I have three halves, where do I mark that on the line?

explain.say: Today we are learning about fractions on a number line. We must divide the line into equal intervals. These equal spaces help us place fractions correctly.

draw.text: Equal intervals on a number line

explain.say: To show fractions, we must make sure the spaces are all the same size. Think of it like cutting a pizza into equal slices. Each slice is one equal interval.
If we divide the space between zero and one into fourths, each space is one fourth. We can then mark the first fourth spot clearly.

items: Divide to 1 into four equal parts

explain.say: Sometimes the fraction is bigger than one. For example, one and a half means one whole space plus another half space. We count the whole spaces first.
To show one and a half, we go past one whole space. We count the whole number one, and then we move another half space further.

items: Move another half space past one

faq.q: What does it mean to divide the line into equal intervals?
faq.a: It means that every space you draw between two numbers must be exactly the same size. If the spaces are not equal, your fraction will be wrong.
asks: How do I make the spaces even?
Are all the gaps on the line the same size?

faq.q: How do I mark a fraction like three quarters?
faq.a: You look at the space between zero and one. If you divide it into four parts, three quarters means you count three of those equal parts from zero.
asks: Where do I put 3/4 on the line?
What does 3/4 look like on a number line?

faq.q: What do I do if the fraction is bigger than one?
faq.a: You must count the whole numbers first. For example, two and a third means you go past two whole spaces, and then you go a little bit more.

faq.q: Do I always start at zero?
faq.a: Yes, when showing a basic fraction, you usually start measuring from zero. This helps everyone know where to begin counting the parts.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fraction and a mixed number?
faq.a: A mixed number like one and a half is the same as an improper fraction like three halves. They both show the same spot on the line.

facts: A number line shows numbers in order from least to greatest.
When dividing a space into equal intervals, each space represents a fraction.
A fraction greater than one means the point is further than one whole unit from zero.
The whole number one is always shown at the mark labeled one.

quiz.say: If you divide the space between zero and one into six equal parts, where would you mark two fifths?

options.show: The mark should be between the second and third lines.
options.say: The mark should be between the second and third lines.

options.show: Marking it exactly in the middle
options.say: Marking it exactly in the middle

quiz.why: The space is divided into six equal parts, so two fifths is not possible. You must use the given division of six parts.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you see the number two, but you must use the denominator given for the division.
wrong.2: This is tempting because two fifths is close to one third, but you must follow the established equal intervals.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it looks like a simple guess, but you must use the fraction given to find the exact spot.

quiz.say: If you mark one and three quarters, which whole number space is it in?

options.show: It is in the space between one and two.
options.say: It is in the space between one and two.

options.show: It is in the space between zero and one.
options.say: It is in the space between zero and one.

quiz.why: Since one whole space is one, and you have three quarters more, you are past one but not yet at two.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might only count the whole number part, but you must count the extra quarters too.
wrong.2: This is tempting because three quarters is close to a whole, but it is not quite enough to reach the next whole number.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the number is less than two, but it is clearly bigger than one.

quiz.say: A point marked at 1 and 1/2 is equivalent to which improper fraction?
quiz.why: One whole is two halves, plus the extra half makes three halves total.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you only counted the whole number part, ignoring the extra half.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you are adding the parts, but the denominator must stay the same for the whole number part.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it is the original form, but the question asks for an improper fraction.
